note: built from the network's schema-4 recorder fixtures (source dbc1d37b): real records, each money kind wrapped in a step; wrong cases are the real pair changed by one field

limits: fill legs name their order by the size the resting order lost in the same step (order_attribution)
realised PnL is recorded for the taker leg only
order_closed.status is inferred: filled / expired / cancelled, with status_basis
a snapshot restore or a dropped view is listed in gaps
balance_change is per account per view pair: the order of effects inside one block is not observable
a balance_change chain breaks at a balance_reset (process start) and at a gap record (dropped view or restore)
move_seq is this node's index of a money move within one run of notes (it restarts when the notes are cleared); it is not a chain sequence number and is not comparable across nodes
a fee_credit record has a leg only for an account whose balance moved: a fee account outside the balance map (the treasury) gets no leg

money_record_kinds.legs: taker and maker: what the match moved each account by
the funding the position paid or got, as applied
the liquidated account's change in the liquidation step, what it returned to the account included (a book step's change is on its fill)
the closed account's change, what it returned to the account included
a deposit credited to its account (legacy op, current-bridge batch credit or bridge v4)
a withdrawal taken from its account, gross (the withdrawal fee included)
a withdrawal returned to its account (held, expired, cancelled, a returned delayed exit, a reclaimed stuck one)
an EVM action that moved USDC between the EVM link and accounts
referral earnings or builder fees paid out to their account
a staker's USDC pay-out from the staking pot (the pot is a leg too)
a treasury transfer to an account, or an account's return to the treasury
a deposit into the liquidity pool
a withdrawal from the liquidity pool
a fee's credits to accounts: the referee discount and the protocol pots, a leg per receiving account
a spot fill: the USDC legs of taker and maker
a vault's idle cash moved into its trading account to place an order
the creation fee taken from the leader
the depositor's deposit (and the vault trading account where it moved)
the payout to the depositor and the leader's profit share
every holder's payout
